arxiv-2004-10270.title: Learnings from Technological Interventions in a Low Resource Language: A Case-Study on Gondi * Equal Contribution Correspondence: kalikab@microsoft.com
arxiv-2004-10270.description: Abstract The primary obstacle to developing technologies for low-resource languages is the lack of usable data. In this paper, we report the adoption and deployment of 4 technology-driven methods of data collection for Gondi, a low-resource vulnerable language spoken by around 2.3 million tribal people in south and central India.

arxiv-2104-09912.title: Investigation of the magnetic ground state of GaV 4 S 8 using powder neutron diffraction Journal: J. Phys.: Condens. Matter
arxiv-2104-09912.creator: S. J. R. Holt, C. Ritter, M. R. Lees, G. Balakrishnan
arxiv-2104-09912.description: Abstract The magnetic ground state of polycrystalline Néel skyrmion hosting material GaV 4 S 8 has been investigated using ac susceptibility and powder neutron diffraction. In the absence of an applied magnetic field GaV 4 S 8 undergoes a transition from a paramagnetic to a cycloidal state below 13 K and then to a ferromagnetic-like state below 6 K.

arxiv-2107-01546.title: Subcritical dynamo and hysteresis in a Babcock-Leighton type kinematic dynamo model
arxiv-2107-01546.creator: Vindya Vashishth, Bidya Binay Karak, Leonid Kitchatinov
arxiv-2107-01546.description: Abstract In Sun and sun-like stars, it is believed that the cycles of the large-scale magnetic field are produced due to the existence of differential rotation and helicity in the plasma flows in their convection zones (CZs). Hence, it is expected that for each star, there is a critical dynamo number for the operation of a large-scale dynamo.

arxiv-2209-09536.title: Towards Task-Prioritized Policy Composition
arxiv-2209-09536.creator: Finn Rietz, Erik Schaffernicht, Todor Stoyanov, Johannes A. Stork
arxiv-2209-09536.description: Abstract Combining learned policies in a prioritized, ordered manner is desirable because it allows for modular design and facilitates data reuse through knowledge transfer. In control theory, prioritized composition is realized by null-space control, where low-priority control actions are projected into the null-space of high-priority control actions. Such a method is currently unavailable for Reinforcement Learning.

arxiv-2210-08245.title: Medial and isospectral algebras
arxiv-2210-08245.creator: Yakov Krasnov, Vladimir G. Tkachev
arxiv-2210-08245.description: Abstract . The purpose of this paper is to give a systematic study of two new classes of commutative nonassociative algebras, the so-called isospectral and medial algebras. An isospectral algebra 𝔸 \mathbb{A} is a generic commutative nonassociative algebra whose idempotents have the same Peirce spectrum.

arxiv-2410-00324.title: Vision Language Models See What You Want but not What You See
arxiv-2410-00324.creator: Qingying Gao, Yijiang Li, Haiyun Lyu, Haoran Sun, Dezhi Luo, Hokin Deng
arxiv-2410-00324.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qingying Gao, Yijiang Li, Haiyun Lyu, Haoran Sun, Dezhi Luo, Hokin Deng. Knowing others’ intentions and taking others’ perspectives are two core components of human intelligence that are considered to be instantiations of theory-of-mind. Infiltrating machines with these abilities is an important step towards building human-level artificial intelligence. Here, to investigate intentionality understanding and level-2 perspective-taking in Vision Language Models (VLMs), we constructed the IntentBench and PerspectBench, which together contains over 300 cognitive experiments grounded in real-world scenarios and classic cognitive tasks.

arxiv-2410-13351.title: Representation Learning of Structured Data for Medical Foundation Models
arxiv-2410-13351.creator: Vijay Prakash Dwivedi, Viktor Schlegel, Andy T. Liu, Thanh-Tung Nguyen, Abhinav Ramesh Kashyap, Jeng Wei, Wei-Hsian Yin, Stefan Winkler, Robby T. Tan
arxiv-2410-13351.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance across various domains, including healthcare. However, their ability to effectively represent structured non-textual data, such as the alphanumeric medical codes used in records like ICD-10 or SNOMED-CT, is limited and has been particularly exposed in recent research.

arxiv-2503-23483.title: Order Independence With Finetuning
arxiv-2503-23483.creator: Katrina Brown Harvard University katrinabrown@college.harvard.edu Reid McIlroy Harvard University reidmcilroy@college.harvard.edu
arxiv-2503-23483.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable performance on many NLP tasks, yet often exhibit order dependence : simply reordering semantically identical tokens (e.g., answer choices in multiple-choice questions) can lead to inconsistent predictions. Recent work proposes Set-Based Prompting (SBP) as a way to remove order information from designated token subsets, thereby mitigating positional biases.

arxiv-2509-16298.title: A global view of diverse construction methods of fuzzy implication functions rooted on F F -chains
arxiv-2509-16298.creator: Raquel Fernandez-Peralta, Juan Vicente Riera
arxiv-2509-16298.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Raquel Fernandez-Peralta, Juan Vicente Riera. Fuzzy implication functions are one of the most important operators used in the fuzzy logic framework. While their flexible definition allows for diverse families with distinct properties, this variety needs a deeper theoretical understanding of their structural relationships. In this work, we focus on the study of construction methods, which employ different techniques to generate new fuzzy implication functions from existing ones. Particularly, we generalize the F F -chain-based construction, recently introduced by Mesiar et al.

pmc-10516226.title: HDAC1 is Involved in Neuroinflammation and Blood-Brain Barrier Damage in Stroke Pathogenesis
pmc-10516226.creator: Hao-Kuang Wang, Yu-Ting Su, Yu-Cheng Ho, Yung-Kuo Lee, Tian-Huei Chu, Kuang-Ti Chen, Cheng-Chun Wu
pmc-10516226.description: BackgroundStroke is a common cause of disability and mortality worldwide; however, effective therapy remains limited. In stroke pathogenesis, ischemia/reperfusion injury triggers gliosis and neuroinflammation that further activates matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), thereby damaging the blood–brain barrier (BBB). Increased BBB permeability promotes macrophage infiltration and brain edema, thereby worsening behavioral outcomes and prognosis.

pmc-11476297.title: Investigating the p21 Ubiquitin-Independent Degron Reveals a Dual Degron Module Regulating p21 Degradation and Function
pmc-11476297.creator: Marianna Riutin, Pnina Erez, Julia Adler, Assaf Biran, Nadav Myers, Yosef Shaul, Alexander E Kalyuzhny
pmc-11476297.description: A group of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are subject to 20S proteasomal degradation in a ubiquitin-independent manner. Recently, we have reported that many IDPs/IDRs are targeted to the 20S proteasome via interaction with the C-terminus of the PSMA3 subunit, termed the PSMA3 Trapper. In this study, we investigated the biological significance of the IDP–Trapper interaction using the IDP p21.

pmc-11499719.title: National Trends in the Prevalence of Self-Perceived Overweight Among Adolescents Between 2005 and 2022: Nationwide Representative Study
pmc-11499719.creator: Jinyoung Jeong, Seungjun Lee, Kyeongmin Lee, Seokjun Kim, Jaeyu Park, Yejun Son, Hyeri Lee, Hayeon Lee, Jiseung Kang, Masoud Rahmati, Damiano Pizzol, Lee Smith, Guillermo F López Sánchez, Elena Dragioti, Guillaume Fond, Laurent Boyer, Selin Woo, Sang Youl Rhee, Dong Keon Yon, Amaryllis Mavragani, Ma
pmc-11499719.description: BackgroundDespite several studies on self-evaluation of health and body shape, existing research on the risk factors of self-perceived overweight is insufficient, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic.ObjectiveThis study aims to identify the risk factors affecting self-perceived overweight and examine how the prevalence of self-perceived overweight has changed before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-11530788.title: Assessment of a training course for cookery students regarding celiac disease and gluten-free diet
pmc-11530788.creator: Maialen Vázquez-Polo, Virginia Navarro, Gesala Perez-Junkera, Arrate Lasa, Idoia Larretxi, Jonatan Miranda, Jon Esparta, Itziar Churruca
pmc-11530788.description: Celiac disease (CD) has a significant impact on the quality of life for those affected, particularly in social settings. One major challenge for these individuals is dining out, as they must constantly avoid cross-contact with gluten, contend with a limited range of restaurant options, and often encounter unknowledgeable or misinformed staff.

pmc-11541951.title: Successful management of a pancreatic mature cystic teratoma with Whipple procedure: A case report
pmc-11541951.creator: Iyad Al Jada, Maaweya Jabareen, Wasef Alhroub, Majd Oweidat
pmc-11541951.description: BackgroundMature cystic teratomas of the pancreas, also known as dermoid cysts, are exceptionally rare tumors characterized by well-differentiated parenchymal tissues. Typically containing diverse tissues from all three germ layers, these teratomas are most commonly found in the ovaries and testes, with infrequent occurrences in the pancreas.

Ribs from young control, old, and streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats were analyzed to quantify both intrinsic and frequency-dependent mechanical properties. Static nanoindentation revealed markedly higher hardness and elastic modulus in the diabetic group (0.47 ± 0.

pmc-12579234.title: Artificial intelligence improves detection and classification of pulmonary venous hypertension related to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction by chest radiography
pmc-12579234.creator: Richard D. White, Mutlu Demirer, Ronnie A. Sebro, Isabel O. Cortopassi, Justin T. Stowell, Matthew R. McCann, Timothy Barry, Christopher P. Appleton, Scott A. Helgeson, Barbaros S. Erdal
pmc-12579234.description: Isolated-Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction [LVDD] ranges (and may progress) from preclinical asymptomatic, symptomatic-LVDD, to LVDD-predominate Heart Failure [HF] presentations; if recognized early, LVDD progression might be preventable. Current early-HF screening remains limited, providing opportunities for insights from a standard Chest X-Ray [CXR].

pmc-12983947.title: Discovery of Four New FGF5 Variants Causing Long Hair in the Dog
pmc-12983947.creator: Robin E. Everts, Tim Roane, Rachael Caron, Cameron Kunstadt, Gabriel Foster, Christa Lafayette
pmc-12983947.description: Simple SummaryThe long-hair phenotype in dogs is a recessive trait and is caused by five known variants in the FGF5 gene. During a standard genotyping procedure, twenty-two Tibetan Mastiffs and one mixed-breed dog were classified as short-haired, even though they phenotypically clearly showed a long hair phenotype.

pmc-13245387.title: Epidemiological characterisation of dengue fever across Saudi Arabia
pmc-13245387.creator: Reem A Bin Suaydan, Waleed S Al Salem, Eitezaz A Zaki, Zenaida S Stead, Lama Alrasheed, Roua A Alsubki
pmc-13245387.description: BackgroundDengue fever is an emerging public health threat in Saudi Arabia. To guide evidence-based vector control, this study aimed to characterise the epidemiological and clinical patterns of infections across key regions in the Kingdom between 2022 and 2024.MethodsA total of 2850 serum samples from suspected dengue patients were collected from hospitals in seven regions in Saudi Arabia.

pmc-13281761.title: A qualitative examination of human papillomavirus vaccine access, beliefs, and behaviors among adult males aged 18–35: applying the Health Stigma and Discrimination Framework
pmc-13281761.creator: Jacquelin I. Cordero, Louis D. Brown, Jesús M. Alemán, María E. Fernández, Serena A. Rodríguez, Eva M. Moya
pmc-13281761.description: BackgroundMales, who disproportionately account for 83% of oropharyngeal cancer cases, are underrepresented in health promotion research, including human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination studies. The initial exclusion of males in HPV vaccine research, policies, and interventions has negatively affected male vaccine uptake. Furthermore, stigma, a well-documented barrier to healthcare engagement, has been overlooked in HPV vaccination behaviors.
